paper.title: Regret Analysis of Stochastic and Nonstochastic Multi-armed Bandit Problems

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic bandit problem (rewards satisfying the psi moment condition)
unmapped: Noise assumption is a general convex log-MGF bound psi (eq. psicond) known to the learner; sub-Gaussian is the special case psi(lambda)=sigma^2 lambda^2/2
settings.definition_quote: There exists a convex function $\psi$ on the reals such that, for all $\lambda \geq 0$, $\ln \E\,e^{\lambda (X-\E[X])} \leq \psi(\lambda)$ and $\ln\,\E\,e^{\lambda (\E[X] - X)} \leq \psi(\lambda)$.
Known parameters: number of arms $K$ and (possibly) number of rounds $n \ge K$. Unknown parameters: $K$ probability distributions $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ on $[0,1]$.
We now show that the result of the previous section is essentially unimprovable when the reward distributions are Bernoulli.

unmapped: Gains/losses in [0,1]; adversary may be non-oblivious
settings.definition_quote: simultaneously, the adversary selects a gain vector $g_t=(g_{1,t},\hdots,g_{K,t}) \in [0,1]^K$, possibly with the help of external randomization; the forecaster receives (and observes) the reward $g_{I_t,t}$, while the gains of the other arms are not observed.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandits with side information (finite context set, adversarial rewards)
unmapped: Regret against best mapping from a finite context set S to arms; context sequence arbitrary but fixed
Variant: class of context sets indexed by Theta, competing with best context set and mapping
settings.definition_quote: The forecaster must learn the best mapping $g : \cS \to \{1,\dots,K\}$ of contexts to arms. We analyze this simple side information setting in the case of adversarial rewards, and we further assume that the sequence of contexts $s_t$ is arbitrary but fixed.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandits with expert advice (adversarial contextual bandit, expert case)
unmapped: Regret against best of N_exp randomized experts whose advice may depend on forecaster's past plays; losses in [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: at each step $t=1,2,\dots$ the forecaster obtains the expert advice $(\xi_t^1,\dots,\xi_t^N)$, where each $\xi_t^j$ is a probability distribution over arms representing the randomized play of expert $j$ at time $t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic contextual bandits with VC policy class (K=2)
unmapped: Regret relative to best policy in class F of VC dimension d_VC
settings.definition_quote: contexts $x_t$ and arm losses $\ell_t = (\ell_{1,t},\dots,\ell_{K,t})$ are realizations of i.i.d. draws from a fixed and unknown distribution $D$ over $\cX \times [0,1]^K$. ... we focus on the case of $K=2$ arms and parametrize classes $\cF$ of policies $f : \cX\to\{1,2\}$ by their VC-dimension $d$

unmapped: Performance measured as expected number of mistakes vs. hinge loss of best linear multiclass classifier U; feedback is only whether prediction was correct
settings.definition_quote: In the bandit version, the learner only observes $\ds1_{\yhat_t \neq y_t}$; that is, whether the prediction at time $t$ was correct or not.

settings.name_in_paper: Online linear optimization with bandit feedback, finite action set (bounded scalar loss)
unmapped: Bounded scalar loss |x^T l| <= 1; N_act = |K| finite actions
settings.definition_quote: we assume that $\cK$ and $\cL$ are such that $|x^{\top} \ell| \leq 1$ for any $(x, \ell) \in \cK \times \cL$. Moreover, we restrict our attention to finite sets $\cK$, with $|\cK| = N$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online combinatorial optimization with semi-bandit feedback
unmapped: Action set C subset of {0,1}^d with ||v||_1 = m; losses in [0,1]^d
settings.definition_quote: the set of arms is $\cC \subseteq \{0,1\}^d$ and the set of linear loss functions is $\cL = [0,1]^d$. We assume $\norm{v}_1 = m$ for all $v\in\cC$ ... after playing $v_t \in \cC$, one observes $(\ell_t(1) v_t(1), \hdots, \ell_t(d) v_t(d))$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online linear optimization with bandit feedback on the Euclidean ball
unmapped: Action set and loss set both the Euclidean unit ball
settings.definition_quote: Let $\cK = \cL = \{x \in \R^d \,:\, \norm{x} \leq 1 \}$ define an online linear optimization problem with bandit feedback.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit convex optimization with two-point feedback
unmapped: Losses convex and differentiable; r B subset K subset R B
settings.definition_quote: at each time step $t$, the forecaster observes the value of a convex and differentiable loss function $\ell_t$ at the played point $x_t$ and at an extra point $x_t'$ of its choice.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit convex optimization with one-point feedback
unmapped: Losses convex and differentiable, uniformly bounded by L_bd (not necessarily in [0,1]); r B subset K subset R B
settings.definition_quote: Let $\cL$ be a set of $G$-Lipschitz differentiable and convex losses, uniformly bounded by $L$ (that is $||\ell||_{\infty} \leq L, \forall \ell \in \cL$).

settings.name_in_paper: Nonlinear stochastic bandits (unimodal mean loss on [0,1])
unmapped: Local inverse-Lipschitz growth condition with constant C_L away from minimizer (eq. strongmax)
settings.definition_quote: If at time $t$ a point $x_t \in [0,1]$ is played, the loss is the realization of an independent random variable $Y_t\in [0,1]$ with expected value $\E[Y_t | x_t] = \mu(x_t)$ ... we assume that $\mu : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ is unimodal, but not necessarily convex.

algorithms.name: OSMD on the Euclidean ball with F(x)=-ln(1-||x||)-||x||

symbols.psi_star: Legendre-Fenchel transform of the log-MGF bound psi

extra_assumptions: reward distributions satisfy the psi moment condition (eq. psicond)

source.label: th:ucb
source.quote: Assume that the reward distributions satisfy \eqref{eq:psicond}. Then $(\alpha, \psi)$-UCB with $\alpha > 2$ satisfies $$\oR_n \leq \sum_{i \,:\, \Delta_i > 0} \left( \frac{\alpha \Delta_i}{\psi^*(\Delta_i / 2)} \ln n + \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 2}  \right)~.$$

results.notes: UCB attributed to Auer et al. (ACF02); survey restates with own proof. Index uses ln t so anytime. Noise mapped to subgaussian but actual condition is general psi.

source.label: eq:regretUCBbounded
source.quote: In case of $[0,1]$-valued random variables, taking $\psi(\lambda) = \tfrac{\lambda^2}{8}$ ... gives $\psi^*(\epsilon) = 2 \epsilon^2$, which in turns gives the following pseudo-regret bound \oR_n \leq \sum_{i : \Delta_i > 0} \left( \frac{2 \alpha}{\Delta_i} \ln n + \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 2}  \right)

results.notes: Corollary of Theorem 2.1 stated in text, not a separate numbered theorem.

extra_assumptions: strategy satisfies E T_i(n) = o(n^a) for all Bernoulli instances, suboptimal arms and a>0

source.label: th:LR85
source.quote: Consider a strategy that satisfies $\E\,T_i(n) = o(n^a)$ for any set of Bernoulli reward distributions, any arm $i$ with $\Delta_i > 0$, and any $a>0$. Then, for any set of Bernoulli reward distributions the following holds $$\liminf_{n \to +\infty} \frac{\oR_n}{\ln n} \geq \sum_{i \,:\, \Delta_i > 0} \frac{\Delta_i}{\kl(\mu_i,\mu^*)}~.$$

results.notes: Extracted from Lai & Robbins (LR85); Bernoulli case only. Proof given for two arms.

source.label: th:Exp3
source.quote: If Exp3 is run with $\eta_t=\eta = \sqrt{\frac{2 \ln K}{n K}}$, then \oR_n \leq \sqrt{2 n K \ln K}~.

results.notes: Exp3 from ACFS03; proof from Bub10. Pseudo-regret holds against any adversary.

source.label: th:Exp3
source.quote: Moeover, if Exp3 is run with $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K}{t K}}$, then \oR_n \leq 2 \sqrt{n K \ln K}~.

results.notes: Anytime version.

source.label: th:exp3P
source.quote: For any given $\delta \in (0,1)$, if Exp3.P is run with $\beta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln(K \delta^{-1})}{n K}}, \eta = 0.95 \sqrt{\frac{\ln(K)}{n K}}, \gamma = 1.05 \sqrt{\frac{K \ln(K)}{n}}$ then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, R_n \leq 5.15 \sqrt{n K \ln(K \delta^{-1})}~.

results.notes: Exp3.P from ACFS03.

source.label: th:exp3P
source.quote: Moreover, if Exp3.P is run with $\beta = \sqrt{\tfrac{\ln(K)}{n K}}$ while $\eta$ and $\gamma$ are chosen as before, then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, R_n \leq \sqrt{\frac{n K}{\ln(K)}} \ln(\delta^{-1}) + 5.15 \sqrt{n K \ln(K)}~.

results.notes: Holds for all confidence levels simultaneously (delta not an input).

source.quote: If Exp3.P is run with $\beta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K }{n K}}, \eta = 0.95 \sqrt{\frac{\ln K }{n K}}, \gamma = 1.05 \sqrt{\frac{K \ln K }{n}}$ then \E\,R_n \leq 5.15 \sqrt{n K \ln K} + \sqrt{\frac{n K}{\ln K }}~.

results.notes: Expected regret against possibly non-oblivious adversary.

extra_assumptions: sup over i.i.d. Bernoulli reward distributions

source.label: th:LBminimax
source.quote: Let $\sup$ be the supremum over all distribution of rewards such that, for $i=1,\dots,K$, the rewards $Y_{i,1},Y_{i,2},\ldots\in\{0,1\}$ are i.i.d., and let $\inf$ be the infimum over all forecasters. Then \inf \sup (...) \geq \frac{1}{20} \sqrt{n K}

results.notes: Minimax lower bound proven in ACFS03; applies to adversarial setting since stochastic is a special case.

source.label: th:context-simple
source.quote: There exists a randomized forecaster for bandits with side information (the $\cS$-Exp3 forecaster, defined in the proof) that satisfies $\oRS_n \le \sqrt{2n |\cS| K\ln K}$ for any set $\cS$ of contexts.

results.notes: Uses tuned Exp3 per context with eta based on n; strictly the proof uses per-context counts n_s with known-horizon tuning, which is glossed over. Attributed to maillard2011adaptive.

source.label: th:Exp4
source.quote: Exp4 without mixing and with $\eta_t=\eta = \sqrt{\frac{2 \ln N}{n K}}$ satisfies \oRx_n \leq \sqrt{2 n N \ln K}~.

results.notes: Recorded exactly as printed; this is almost certainly a typo for sqrt(2 n K ln N) (the proof yields ln N/eta + (K/2) n eta and the text says the bound is of order sqrt(nK ln N)).

source.label: th:Exp4
source.quote: On the other hand, with $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\ln N}{t K}}$ it satisfies \oRx_n \leq 2 \sqrt{n N \ln K}~.

results.notes: As printed; likely typo for 2 sqrt(n K ln N).

source.label: th:exp4-mixing
source.quote: Exp4 with mixing coefficient $\gamma$ and with $\eta_t = \eta = \gamma/K$ satisfies \oRx_n \le \frac{\gamma\,n}{2} + \frac{K\ln N}{\gamma}~.

results.notes: Proof sketched as modification of ACFS03 Theorem 7.1. Theorem numbering inferred.

extra_assumptions: regret against best context set and best mapping

source.label: th:theta-regret
source.quote: There exists a randomized forecaster achieving \oR^{\Theta}_n = \mathcal{O}\left(n^{2/3}\left(\max_{\theta\in\Theta}|\cS_{\theta}|K\ln K\right)^{1/3}\sqrt{\ln|\Theta|}\right) for any class of context sets.

results.notes: Exp4 over S-Exp3 experts; from maillard2011adaptive. Theorem number inferred.

extra_assumptions: binary policy class of VC dimension d_VC

source.quote: For any class $\cF$ of binary policies $f : \cX\to\{0,1\}$ of VC-dimension $d$ and for all $n > d$, the forecaster VE run with $n' = \sqrt{n\left(2d\ln\frac{en}{d}+ \ln\frac{3}{\delta}\right)}$ satisfies \sum_{t=1}^n \ell_{I_t,t} - n\inf_{f\in\cF}\ell_D(f) \leq c\sqrt{n\left(d\ln\frac{en}{d} + \ln\frac{3}{\delta}\right)} for some constant $c > 0$ and with probability at least $1-\delta$

results.notes: Unspecified constant c, recorded as O. Regret vs risk of best policy (n*l_D(f*)). From beygelzimer2011contextual. Compute not stated (enumerates F').

bound.regime: eta = sqrt(ln N/(3nd)), gamma = eta d

source.label: th:exp2john
source.quote: For any $\eta,\gamma > 0$ such that ${\eta d} \le {\gamma}$, Exp2 with John's exploration satisfies $$\oR_n \leq 2 \gamma n + \frac{\ln N}{\eta} + \eta n d~.$$ In particular, with $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln N}{3 n d}}$ and $\gamma = \eta d$, $$\oR_n \leq 2 \sqrt{3 n d \ln N}~.$$

results.notes: From BCK12. Paper notes discretization-based strategies are often not computationally efficient.

source.label: th:osmdnegent
source.quote: For any set $\cC\subseteq\{0,1\}^d$, if OSMD is run on $\cK=\conv(\cC)$ with $F(x) = \sum_{i=1}^d x_i \ln x_i - \sum_{i=1}^d x_i$ ... In particular, with the estimate \eqref{eq:semibanditestimate} and $\eta= \sqrt{\frac{2m}{nd}\ln\frac{d}{m}}$, $$\oR_n \leq  \sqrt{2 m d n \ln \frac{d}{m}}~.$$

results.notes: From ABL11. Projection may be inefficient for some C, so compute not stated. Theorem number inferred.

source.label: th:osmdzero
source.quote: In particular, choosing the $0$-potential $\psi(x) = (- x)^{-q}$, the estimate~\eqref{eq:semibanditestimate}, and $\eta= \sqrt{\frac{2}{q-1} \frac{m^{1 - 2/q}}{d^{1 - 2/q}}}$, $$\oR_n \leq q \sqrt{\frac{2}{q-1} m d n}~.$$

results.notes: Stated eta does not depend on n, which looks like a typo; recorded bound as stated. For m=1 gives log-free MAB bound (INF).

source.label: th:osmdzero
source.quote: With $q=2$ this gives $$\oR_n \leq 2 \sqrt{2 m d n}~.$$

results.notes: With m=1, d=K this is the log-free adversarial MAB bound 2 sqrt(2Kn).

bound.regime: gamma = 1/sqrt(n), eta = sqrt(ln n/(2nd)), eta d <= 1/2

source.label: th:two-point
source.quote: Let $\cK\subseteq\R^d$ be a closed convex set such that $r\,\Ball\subseteq\cK\subseteq R\,\Ball$ ... \oR_n \le \frac{R^2}{\eta} + \eta (Gd)^2 n + \delta\left(3 + \frac{R}{r} \right) G n~. source.quote: For any unimodal and $C_H$-Lipschitz mean loss function $\mu : [0,1] \to [0,1]$ that satisfies~(\ref{eq:strongmax}), if the SGS algorithm is run with $\ve_s = C_L\varphi^{-(s+3)}$ then \oR_n \le \frac{C_H}{C_L^2}8\varphi^6\ln(6n) \left[ \frac{2\varphi}{\varphi-1}\sqrt{1 + C_L^2 n} + \frac{1}{4}\log_{\phi}^2\bigl(1 + C_L^2 n\bigr) \right]~.
